- [ ] For performance/data claims, freeze workload/source identities before tuning, compare with an independent oracle, and report actual limits and unsuccessful trials.
- [ ] Update user-facing documentation and the architecture tracker; do not equate finite passing tests with universal correctness or security.

Baseline: [architecture source](https://github.com/anthonykewl20/GoPyt/blob/feat/atomic-data-backends/docs/architecture-programme.md). Existing implementation and measurements: #1.
title: [P0] Freeze production workload, threat model, and qualification targets

body:
This is the complete tracked set of known architectural gaps from the repository programme and security/production boundaries. Scope: GoPyT language, runtime, Guard and tools. Model training is excluded.

Milestone: https://github.com/anthonykewl20/GoPyt/milestone/1

Existing partial implementation: #1. Atomic batches, database namespace policy, maintenance key rotation and real retail trials are implemented on that draft PR branch. They do not close the broader architecture gates.

Execution order: define workload/threat targets first; implement P0 foundations and their dependencies; develop the P1 data/execution/Guard capabilities; complete tooling and IPC qualification; finish sustained recovery qualification and independent review. Priorities do not override the dependency links.

Master checklist

- [ ] #3 [P0] Freeze production workload, threat model, and qualification targets
- [ ] #4 [P0] Complete resource-scoped capabilities and delegation
- [ ] #5 [P0] Define and enforce buffer, view, and resource lifetimes
- [ ] #6 [P0] Provide and qualify OS isolation for hostile execution
- [ ] #7 [P0] Complete transaction, retry, and failure semantics
- [ ] #8 [P1] Replace the bounded snapshot bottleneck with scalable secure storage
- [ ] #9 [P1] Add typed data schemas, migrations, and query boundaries
- [ ] #10 [P0] Implement user and tenant authorization boundaries
- [ ] #11 [P0] Complete credential lifecycle and encrypted data migration
- [ ] #12 [P0] Detect replay of old authenticated storage snapshots
- [ ] #13 [P0] Unify cancellation, deadlines, backpressure, and shutdown
- [ ] #14 [P1] Integrate stateful and effectful acceptance into GoPyT Guard
- [ ] #15 [P1] Extend Guard protection across dependency graphs and evolution
- [ ] #16 [P1] Establish a compiled execution path with semantic conformance
- [ ] #17 [P1] Specify exact numerical, monetary, and time semantics
- [ ] #18 [P1] Implement bounded typed streaming and safe columnar/mapped access
- [ ] #19 [P2] Qualify shared-memory IPC and matrix interoperability
- [ ] #20 [P2] Build dependency-aware semantic editor tooling
- [ ] #21 [P1] Add safe production observability and language debugging/profiling
- [ ] #22 [P1] Define package, bytecode, native ABI, and upgrade compatibility
- [ ] #23 [P0] Harden release and build supply-chain integrity
- [ ] #24 [P0] Qualify HTTP transport, gateway, and deployment security
- [ ] #25 [P0] Run sustained real-data, failure, and disaster-recovery qualification
- [ ] #26 [P0] Complete independent security review and production release gates

Coverage map

- Resource capabilities: authority and OS isolation.
- Resource lifetimes: safe buffers/views and task/native cleanup.
- Transactional data: transaction semantics, scalable persistence and schema migration.
- Identity and keys: tenant authorization, credential lifecycle and rollback protection.
- Stateful Guard: effectful transition/fault acceptance and dependency closure.
- Execution: concurrency/deadlines and a conformant compiled execution path.
- Data interfaces: numeric/time semantics, streaming/columnar access and IPC/matrix boundaries.
- Tooling: semantic editor support, debugging/profiling, package compatibility and secure releases.
- Cross-cutting qualification: workload/threat targets, HTTP/gateway security, sustained real-data/recovery tests and independent review.

Closure rules

- Every child issue must satisfy its acceptance checklist and link retained evidence; discovery of further gaps adds issues here rather than silently narrowing scope.
- Keep distinct: implemented behavior, measured behavior, untested assumptions and deployment responsibilities.
- A milestone completion date is intentionally unset until workload targets and delivery capacity are established.
- No claim of universal security, zero possible defects or production readiness follows merely from issue closure or benchmark scores. Production claims must match the qualified workload and documented threat boundary.

Sources: [architecture programme](https://github.com/anthonykewl20/GoPyt/blob/feat/atomic-data-backends/docs/architecture-programme.md), [security scope](https://github.com/anthonykewl20/GoPyt/blob/feat/atomic-data-backends/SECURITY.md), [validation report](https://github.com/anthonykewl20/GoPyt/blob/feat/atomic-data-backends/docs/architecture-validation-2026-09-09.md).
